title: Rent control
description: DRAFT for the owner's review (plan step 17, scenario scrutiny): the 'leans' values in this file are a first draft, not an authoritative coding of any position. Convention: -1 is left-coded, +1 is right-coded, 0 is no clear coding. compass.economic: -1 more state role in the economy, +1 more free-market; compass.social: -1 more socially liberal, +1 more socially traditional; us_partisan.party: -1 aligned with the Democratic Party, +1 with the Republican Party.
proposition: Cities should cap how much landlords can raise rents each year.
opposing_position: Cities should not cap how much landlords can raise rents each year.

economic.rationale: Supporters usually favour public rules that limit what private landlords may charge, which is a larger state role in the housing market.

social.rationale: The position is mostly economic; the link to social questions is weak, with a slight lean to protecting existing tenants and neighbourhoods.

party.rationale: In US politics, rent regulation is more often backed by Democratic officials and platforms than by Republican ones.

economic.rationale: Opponents usually argue that prices should be set by supply and demand and that caps reduce the housing supply.

social.rationale: The position is mostly economic; the link to social questions is weak.

party.rationale: In US politics, opposition to rent regulation is more often voiced by Republican officials, though many Democrats also object.

title: Drug decriminalization
description: Seeded topic used in the political-direction pairs of the golden set. Leans are a draft for the owner's review.
proposition: Possession of small amounts of illegal drugs for personal use should be decriminalized.
opposing_position: Possession of small amounts of illegal drugs for personal use should not be decriminalized.

economic.rationale: The position is not mainly about the economy; some supporters stress public spending on treatment and others stress lower enforcement costs.

social.rationale: Supporters usually treat drug use as a health and personal-freedom matter rather than a crime, which is typically coded as socially liberal.

party.rationale: In US politics, decriminalization is more often backed by Democrats, though some Republicans and libertarians support it too.

economic.rationale: The position is not mainly about the economy; it is chiefly about law enforcement and public order.

social.rationale: Opponents usually stress criminal penalties as a deterrent and traditional public-order values, which is typically coded as socially conservative.

party.rationale: In US politics, keeping criminal penalties is more often backed by Republicans, though some Democrats agree.

title: Sanctuary cities
description: Seeded topic used in the political-direction pairs of the golden set. Leans are a draft for the owner's review.
proposition: Cities should limit their local police's cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.
opposing_position: Cities should not limit their local police's cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.

economic.rationale: The position concerns immigration and policing more than the economy; supporters often also stress the role of immigrant workers in local economies.

social.rationale: Supporters usually favour more permissive immigration policy and stress trust between immigrant communities and local police.

party.rationale: In US politics, sanctuary policies are more often backed by Democratic officials than by Republican ones.

economic.rationale: The position concerns immigration and law enforcement more than the economy; some opponents stress public costs.

social.rationale: Opponents usually favour stricter immigration enforcement and full cooperation between local and federal authorities.

party.rationale: In US politics, opposition to sanctuary policies is more often voiced by Republican officials than by Democratic ones.
